newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian sorghum demand seen staying flat.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian sorghum demand seen staying flat.

text.p: There was little to suggest that sorghum demand in Australia would pick up considerably in the near-term, Queensland grain cooperative Grainco said in its weekly market report.
The majority of end-users appeared to have coverage through to the new crop while the quantity of frost damage to wheat in both southern and central Queensland was still unknown, it said.

Grainco said the next couple of weeks could be interesting in the sorghum market with the direction of the Australian dollar still undecided and with continuing talk of another interest rate cut possibly putting downward pressure on the currency.
Added to this, the U.S. corn crop was entering its harvest period while the stocks were possibly being tightened by unfavourable harvest weather.
"(The) near-term price direction is uncertain still," Grainco's trading manager Rob Brealey said in the report.
Domestic demand for feed barley continued relatively quiet in the past week, the Grainco report said.
Domestic consumers were likely to remain on the sidelines until the full extent of frost damage to the wheat crop could be put into perspective, it said.
Domestic malting barley values remained competitive with wheat prices, the report said.
A flurry of activity was seen in the domestic cottonseed market over the past week, it said.
With ginning drawing to a close in coming weeks, both domestic and export consumers had shown increased interest in securing any remaining uncommitted grower seed, it said.
Soyoil prices were receivinfg support from higher palm oil prices as a result of strong exports.
Domestic sunflower values were steady over the past week, it said.
